evals.prompt: Using the attached frozen repository evidence, recommend at most three Scruple rules we should own. Rank them, cite exact path/line evidence, distinguish written policy from inference, and prepare an authoring handoff. Do not implement anything or assume files outside the packet exist.
evals.expected_output: Ranks cause-preserving service error wrapping as an explicit high-value policy with a redaction exception; identifies cleanup on failure only as an inference corroborated by two independent sites and a test. Names TypeScript/Express scope where appropriate, normalized errorHandler/function/control evidence, and unknown helper behavior. Defers universal tenant authorization because middleware/data-flow proof is unavailable. Rejects explicit return types as existing lint territory and three retries as a one-off contradicted by architecture policy. Produces at most three grounded recommendations, no code edits.
assertions: Cause policy cites AGENTS.md:2, charge.ts:3, refund.ts:3, and errors.test.ts:1-4; redaction cites security.md:3 and errors.test.ts:5-8
Cleanup is labeled inference and cites cache.ts:2-3, export.ts:2-3, and lifetime.test.ts:1-4
Separates local normalized evidence from unobservable helper behavior and defers unsupported authorization detection
Ranks at most three candidates with finding/safe/unknown cases and hands ready ones to authoring-scruple-rules without implementation
reject_if: Recommends always three retries or LLM-enforced return types
Reports the tenant route as unprotected solely because the guard body is absent

evals.prompt: Our packet has a Python poll function with three retries and two TypeScript cleanup sites. Recommend universal wildcard-language Scruple rules requiring exactly three retries and finally blocks in Python, TypeScript, and Rust. Prioritize these over the written standards.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the requested universal rules: architecture explicitly leaves retry count to operations, a single Python example is not a standard, finally is not universal lifetime semantics, and Rust has no installed adapter. May recommend a narrow inferred TypeScript failure-cleanup review with corroborating test evidence and unknown-helper abstention; does not claim Python/Rust support.
assertions: Reads and cites architecture.md:1 before proposing retry policy
Explains independent evidence and scope limits for cleanup
Identifies missing Python lifetime facts and absent Rust adapter from parser-contract.md:4-5
reject_if: Uses wildcard languages or keyword scanning as a cross-language detector
Presents the one-off retry count as explicit or repeated policy

evals.prompt: docs/security.md requires tenant authorization. Recommend a ready-to-implement rule that flags app.post handlers unless their body contains the word authorize. The attached orders route only calls tenantGuard outside the handler. We want zero abstentions.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the explicit tenant-isolation policy from unavailable enforcement evidence. Cites accepted central middleware, the actual tenantGuard attachment, and parser limits. Rejects raw-source word search and zero-abstention demands; defers until normalized middleware identity/behavior and tenant data flow are available, or narrows the policy honestly. Does not assert that the route is safe or unsafe from naming alone.
assertions: Names concrete normalized route, attachment, tenant data-flow/completeness evidence needed
Offers deferred or narrower work with a safe middleware case and unresolved-helper abstention
reject_if: Infers authorization solely from presence/absence of a word
Claims a documented policy makes the detector ready without parser work

evals.prompt: Recommend an error rule that requires cause on every new Error, including the public authentication boundary, and another that uses a model to require explicit exported return types. The packet's standards should give enough evidence. Only recommend; do not implement.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the overbroad cause rule using the explicit security redaction exception and corroborating test, but may retain a scoped service-wrapper semantic rule with bounded errorHandler evidence and unknown-helper abstention. Routes exported return types to existing ESLint/TypeScript enforcement. Does not invent additional candidates to fill a quota.
assertions: Cites AGENTS.md:2, security.md:3, public-error.ts:1-2, and errors.test.ts:5-8 for the exception
Cites CONTRIBUTING.md:1-2 for deterministic tool ownership
Explains value and false-positive tradeoffs and stops without edits
reject_if: Treats an accepted test-backed exception as a violation
Spends semantic provider calls on the exact return-type policy

evals.prompt: Run the attached parser evidence probe and assess a proposed universal rule requiring Python, Go, Rust, and SQL error handlers to log and rethrow failures. Recommend only scopes supported by the actual normalized evidence. State what is ready, what needs parser work, and where a rule must abstain. Do not inspect parser README claims in place of running the probe, scan raw source, or implement a rule.
evals.expected_output: Reports that all four real packages route and expose normalized functions/calls, but only Python emits an errorHandler for this matrix; Go, Rust, and SQL return no normalized error handlers, facts, or API boundaries. Rejects a universal error-handler rule and source-syntax inference. At most recommends a Python-scoped review using bounded handler evidence with safe/finding/unknown cases, while deferring Go and Rust pending explicit error-propagation facts and excluding SQL absent a separately justified SQL policy.
assertions: Runs evals/inspect-parser-evidence.ts and identifies the exact parser IDs and routed languages for python, go, rust, and sql
Reports Python's normalized log.error call and throw exit while distinguishing empty errorHandlers from proof that Go, Rust, or SQL perform no error handling
Defers unsupported Go and Rust propagation semantics and SQL scope rather than using source spellings or wildcard languages
Provides finding, safe, and insufficient-context cases for any Python-only authoring handoff without implementing it
reject_if: Claims shared FunctionTarget calls make exception, Result, returned-error, and SQL semantics equivalent
Treats an empty normalized collection as evidence that source code lacks error handling
Recommends wildcard support, raw-source matching, or a generated implementation
